item.title: Cryptographic Issues in Cloudflare's Circl FourQ Implementation (CVE-2025-8556)
item.description:
📝 FourQ is an elliptic curve with 128-bit security, developed by Microsoft Research and is defined by a twisted Edwards curve equation. In addition, the FourQ curve defines two endomorphisms, or structure-preserving functions, which serve as "shortcuts" to perform computations on the curve more efficiently. Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman or ECDH involves each side taking a secret scalar \(k\) and multiplying it with a fixed generator point \(G\) to compute the point \(Q = k*G\).
🔗 Read more: https://www.botanica.software/blog/cryptographic-issues-in-cloudflares-circl-fourq-implementation

item.title: Linux Capabilities Revisited
item.description:
📝 Backdooring Python The command setcap sets file capabilities on an executable. Enumerating all binaries with capabilities set is possible with the command getcap -r: # getcap -r / 2>/dev/null /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/gstreamer1. 12 cap_setuid=ep Inside the /proc directory: # cat /proc/1143966/status | grep Cap where: CapInh = Inherited capabilities CapPrm = Permitted capabilities CapEff = Effective capabilities CapBnd = Bounding set CapAmb = Ambient capabilities set Utilising the command capsh, we decode the capabilities as follows: # capsh --decode=0000000000000080 0x0000000000000080=cap_setuid Or with the command getpcaps, passing the PID as an argument: # getpcaps 1143966 Capabilities for `1143966': = cap_setuid+ep Remove the capabilities from a binary with setcap -r # setcap -r /usr/bin/python3.
🔗 Read more: https://dfir.ch/posts/linux_capabilities/

item.title: The security paradox of local LLMs
item.description:
📝 When attackers prompt them to include vulnerabilities, local models comply with up to 95% success rate. We present two ways attackers can exploit local LLMs to generate malicious code. The second forces immediate code execution during your AI-assisted coding session.

item.title: Tesla Recalls Almost 13,000 EVs over Risk of Battery Power Loss
item.description:
📝 IndustriesTransportationFacebookXLinkedInEmailLinkGiftExpandA vehicle transport truck with Tesla Model Y vehicles at the company's store in Colma, California. The problem stems from a faulty battery pack connection part, which can lead to loss of propulsion without warning, Tesla said in documents posted to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s website. The company is recalling almost 8,000 Model Y SUVs and just over 5,000 Model 3 sedans produced from March through August of this year.
